chunks: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from one of his companions, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why did Allah forbid alcohol, carrion, blood, and pork?'

He said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not forbid that to His servants out of desire for what He forbade them, nor out of asceticism for what He permitted them. Rather, He created the creation and knew what sustains their bodies and what benefits them. So Allah permitted and allowed them, out of His grace, for their benefit. And He knew what harms them, so He forbade them from it and made it haram. Then He allowed it for the needy, permitting it in the time when the body cannot function without it, so He commanded him to take from it only as much as is sufficient, and no more than that.'

Then he said: 'As for eating carrion, no one approaches it, and whoever eats from it, his body weakens, his frame wastes away, his strength vanishes, his lineage is cut off, and the eater of carrion does not die except suddenly.'

As for blood, it causes the eater to have yellow bile, bad breath, foul odor, and a bad temperament. It gives him the 'bite' (aggression) and hardness of the heart, and lack of compassion and mercy, so that one cannot be sure he will not kill his son or his father. Nor can one be sure regarding his close relative or anyone who accompanies him.

As for pork, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, transformed a people into various forms resembling pigs, monkeys, bears, and other transformed creatures. Then He forbade eating its like so that benefit would not be derived from them, and His punishment would not be underestimated.
As for alcohol, He forbade it because of its action and its corruption.

He said: 'The one who is addicted to alcohol is like the worshipper of an idol. It causes tremors, removes his light (of reason), destroys his dignity, and drives him to dare upon the prohibitions, such as shedding blood and committing adultery. One cannot be sure that when he is drunk he will not pounce on his family, while he does not comprehend it. And alcohol will only add to its drinker every evil.'

key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْأَصْفَر: Yellow bile (a humoral cause of temperament)
key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: Carrion (meat of an animal that died naturally)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual reasons behind the Islamic prohibition of alcohol, blood, carrion, and pork?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that divine prohibitions are rooted in empirical wisdom rather than mere decree, detailing how carrion, blood, pork, and alcohol specifically degrade physical vitality and spiritual character. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for linking *hikmah* (wisdom) to *hukm* (ruling), emphasizing that the prohibition of alcohol is due to its inherent corruption of reason and dignity, which serves as the gateway to major sins like murder and adultery. The text also highlights the concept of *al-mukhbar* (the compelled) allowing for limited consumption when necessary for bodily survival, reinforcing the principle of preserving life.
